hero.subtitle: NodeChart is a browser-first workspace for CEX and DEX charts. Market data comes from public providers where reachable; CORS, region, rate limits and outages can affect feeds. Most requests stay in your browser; one narrow route obtains KuCoin's public WebSocket token. Optional ads and tips support the app; no paid subscription is required in the current version.

features.heading: Charting and analysis tools in one browser workspace.
features.subheading: Chart calculations run in your browser; public market data and page assets still depend on the network and provider availability.

items.title: Client-side by design
items.body: Chart and indicator calculations run in your browser. Public market-data requests still depend on provider rate limits, CORS and regional access. No paid subscription is required in the current release.

items.title: CEX and DEX in one grid
items.body: Compare a Binance perpetual with a Uniswap pool side by side. One instrument model covers centralized order books and on-chain liquidity.

items.title: Multi-chart layouts
items.body: Switch between 1x1, 2x1 and 2x2 grids. Every pane keeps its own symbol and persists across reloads.

items.title: Local workspace settings
items.body: No account is required. Your watchlist and layout are stored in localStorage, and optional Adsterra delivery scripts are not loaded unless you allow them. Market-data requests still go to external providers when you use those features.

items.title: Five languages, real SEO
items.body: German, English, Spanish, Mandarin and Russian — each prerendered as static HTML with its own canonical URL and hreflang.

items.title: Edge-first infrastructure
items.body: Static pages are delivered through Cloudflare's edge network, and locale routing is resolved at the edge.

items.title: Bar replay on every timeframe
items.body: Replay 1m candles with play, pause, step and 10× speed. Indicators, volume profile and support/resistance recalculate over the visible candle slice; source data is unchanged.

items.title: Strategy lab
items.body: Run six local backtests with fees and mark-to-market results. Outcomes depend on the candle history and assumptions; they do not predict future performance.

items.title: Screener for provider-listed USDT pairs
items.body: Browse the latest provider-listed USDT spot tickers (Gate primary, OKX fallback) by volume, reported 24 h change or range. Filter, search, open ad-hoc charts and export CSV; listings and fields vary.

items.title: Browser-stored watchlist
items.body: Saved symbols have no in-app count cap, but available storage depends on the browser. CEX quotes appear only when their base is present in the shared Gate/OKX spot-ticker snapshot, normally cached for up to two minutes; last displayed values can remain if refresh fails. DEX entries are not quoted here, and this is not a per-symbol live stream.

items.title: Risk & position calculator
items.body: Enter account size, risk %, entry, stop and target to calculate position size, notional, margin and R:R. It is a calculation aid, not a recommendation or guarantee.

items.title: CSV export & axis modes
items.body: Export OHLCV and screener snapshots as CSV, use log/percent axes, see a bar-close countdown and switch to baseline charts.

items.title: Chart pattern detection
items.body: Double tops, head and shoulders, triangles and flags are detected over the visible candle buffer and shown with a heuristic confidence score. The score describes pattern fit, not the probability of a future move.

items.title: MTF technicals matrix
items.body: Summarizes 14 oscillator and moving-average signals across six timeframes using loaded data. It is a technical summary, not a trading recommendation; freshness depends on its data source.

items.title: Market heatmap + bar magnifier
items.body: Provider-listed USDT pairs as a treemap (area = reported volume, colour = reported 24 h change), plus trade detail and taker delta for selected candles when the feed supports them. Click a tile to open its chart.

items.title: Trade journal with stats
items.body: Record trades locally with win rate, profit factor, expectancy, average R, tags and CSV export. Metrics reflect the entries you record.

items.title: Custom indicator formulas
items.body: Write and test per-candle formulas, import text from GitHub over HTTPS and plot a line or price overlay. Formulas execute in this page without a secure sandbox; run only code you trust. Available without a scripting subscription in this release.

items.title: Help for every indicator & metric
items.body: Documentation for 34 indicators, 42 market metrics and Script Lab is searchable and filterable across five locales.

items.title: The Edge Suite
items.body: The Edge Suite combines candle-based liquidation estimates, historical lead/lag statistics, market-regime summaries and hourly/weekday patterns. Inputs and coverage vary; these outputs are descriptive research aids, not predictions.

topics.question: What exactly is NodeChart?
topics.answer: NodeChart is a free-to-use, browser-first charting workspace for crypto markets. It combines configured CEX adapters and DEX-provider data in one interface. Most processing and storage are client-side; a narrow same-origin route obtains KuCoin's public WebSocket token. Public feeds can be partial or unavailable depending on provider, browser and region.

topics.question: Do I need an account or an API key?
topics.answer: No. NodeChart never asks for exchange credentials or user-provided API keys. Most public data calls go from your browser to exchanges and data providers; a narrow same-origin route only obtains KuCoin's public WebSocket token. Providers may apply rate limits, CORS rules and regional restrictions.

topics.question: How do I switch between the 1x1, 2x1 and 2x2 layouts?
topics.answer: Use the layout switcher in the terminal toolbar, or press 1, 2 or 3 on your keyboard. Your choice is written to the global store and persisted in localStorage, so it survives a page reload.

topics.question: How do I change the symbol I am watching?
topics.answer: Open the symbol search in the terminal sidebar and pick an instrument. Each pane can carry its own symbol; the first pane follows the globally active token. In a multi-pane layout you can therefore compare, for example, BTC on Binance against WBTC on Ethereum.

topics.question: Which timeframes and chart types are supported?
topics.answer: Timeframes run from 1 minute to 1 week (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d, 1w). Chart types include candles, bars, line, area and Heikin-Ashi. All of them are rendered on canvas for smooth panning and zooming.

topics.question: Where does the price data come from?
topics.answer: Market data uses public CEX and DEX-provider endpoints, mostly called by your browser. A narrow same-origin route only obtains KuCoin's public WebSocket token. Provider CORS, IP-based rate limits, regional rules and outages can affect results; browser-local budgets cannot coordinate users sharing an upstream IP. Candle history may come from a labeled alternative venue or labeled stale cache.

topics.question: Does NodeChart store my data?
topics.answer: Theme, language, layout, watchlist and active symbol are stored in this browser. The ad choice is also stored locally for up to six months. Optional Adsterra scripts load only after you allow them; market-data providers and the host may process technical request data such as IP addresses. There is no user-account database.

topics.question: A chart is empty or not updating.
topics.answer: A browser extension, network rule or regional/provider restriction may block the selected exchange API or WebSocket. Check whether the relevant market-data endpoint is reachable, or try another instrument or source. Ad preferences are separate: you do not have to allow ads to use charts.

topics.question: How do I change the theme or the language?
topics.answer: Both sit in the header. The theme button cycles through Acid Green, Electric Purple and Daylight; the language menu switches the locale while keeping you on the same page. Your system language is detected automatically on the first visit.

funding.name: Perpetual funding rate
funding.body: Periodic payment between long and short positions in a perpetual-futures contract. A positive rate generally means longs pay shorts; a negative rate, shorts pay longs. This venue snapshot does not predict price direction.

annual.name: Simple annualized funding rate
annual.body: Current funding rate annualised using the provider-reported interval (simple rate × periods per year). This compares the current rate; it is not a forecast or compounded return.

mark.name: Venue mark price
mark.body: Venue-calculated reference price used by its margin and liquidation rules. It can differ from the last trade; formulas vary by exchange and it does not prevent losses.

premium.name: Mark/index difference
premium.body: Difference between mark and index prices, shown as a percentage. It describes the current snapshot; its sign alone does not establish buying or selling pressure.

oi.name: Open-interest notional
oi.body: Reported open-interest notional from OKX or Gate where available. Changes describe outstanding contracts in that source; they do not confirm a price trend.

lsrAcc.name: Long/short accounts
lsrAcc.body: Ratio of reported long- to short-oriented accounts in this feed. Some traders use extreme readings as contrarian context; the ratio alone does not indicate future direction.

lsrTaker.name: Long/short taker volume
lsrTaker.body: Ratio of aggressive buys to sells in the reported feed. Above 1 means reported buy-initiated volume exceeded sell-initiated volume in that snapshot; it does not predict price direction.

lsrTop.name: Top-trader positioning
lsrTop.body: Reported long/short ratio for the largest accounts in this feed. Differences from other groups describe positioning, not a standalone contrarian signal.

liq5m.name: Reported liquidations (5 min)
liq5m.body: Provider-reported long and short positions liquidated in the last five minutes. The snapshot may be incomplete and does not imply a cascade or reversal.

nextFunding.name: Next funding settlement
nextFunding.body: Time remaining until the next reported funding settlement. This countdown alone does not imply a price move.

spread.name: Bid-ask spread
spread.body: Difference between the best bid and ask. A narrow spread may mean lower quoted costs for small trades, but does not measure order-book depth or execution quality.

imbalance.name: Order-book imbalance
imbalance.body: Share of buy versus sell notional in the visible order-book snapshot. Displayed depth can change or be cancelled and is not a guarantee of executable liquidity.

cvd.name: Cumulative volume delta
cvd.body: Running sum of aggressive buys minus sells in the selected feed. A divergence from price describes a difference in observed flow; it does not confirm conviction or predict a reversal.

delta60.name: Short-window taker delta
delta60.body: Short-window difference between aggressive buy and sell volume in the selected feed. It summarizes recent prints; it does not identify trader intent or predict momentum.

depth.name: Reported book depth
depth.body: Cumulative notional shown on each side of the reported order book around the mid-price. Displayed depth may change or be cancelled before execution.

mcap.name: Reported market capitalisation
mcap.body: Provider-reported total market capitalisation for its tracked assets. Coverage and calculation methods depend on the provider.

btcD.name: Bitcoin dominance
btcD.body: BTC's reported share of total market capitalisation. Changes can coincide with market rotations, but dominance alone does not identify their cause or direction.

ethD.name: Ethereum dominance
ethD.body: ETH's reported share of total market capitalisation. Track it as descriptive context alongside BTC dominance; it does not identify the cause or direction of a rotation.

fng.name: Fear & Greed index
fng.body: Sentiment score from 0–100 built from volatility, momentum, dominance and social data. Extreme readings describe sentiment context; they are not entry or exit signals.

dvol.name: Deribit implied-volatility index (DVOL)
dvol.body: Deribit's options-derived implied-volatility index for BTC and ETH; the 24-hour change compares index readings. Implied volatility reflects option pricing, not realised volatility or a forecast.

putCall.name: Call/put open-interest ratio
putCall.body: Calls divided by puts in Deribit's reported BTC options open interest. The ratio describes that provider snapshot; it does not reveal trader intent or predict direction.

maxPain.name: Max pain
maxPain.body: Strike with the lowest modelled intrinsic payout across reported BTC option open interest. This snapshot-based calculation is not a price target or forecast.

smile.name: IV smile
smile.body: Implied volatility across strikes for the selected expiry. The shape describes quoted option pricing; it does not establish trader motives or forecast price moves.

term.name: IV term structure
term.body: Implied volatility across available expiries. The shape depends on the listed contracts and provider snapshot; contango or backwardation is not a forecast.

advPct.name: Advancer share
advPct.body: Share of returned USDT spot pairs with a known 24 h change that are up. This is a venue-snapshot signal; the 25%/75% thresholds are heuristics, not a market-wide reading.

median.name: Median 24h change
median.body: Median reported 24 h change among pairs with a known value in the current provider snapshot. It is less sensitive to outliers than a mean, but the sample is not the whole market.

vp.name: Volume profile (VR)
vp.body: Estimates volume distribution by price from candles in the visible range. The point of control is the bin with the highest calculated volume in that sample; it does not predict future price behaviour.

avwap.name: Anchored VWAP
avwap.body: Volume-weighted average price from your chosen anchor, based on loaded candles. It is a comparison reference and cannot identify which traders are in profit.

sr.name: NodeCluster
sr.body: NodeCluster groups nearby swing pivots from chart candles into layered support/resistance bands. Node markers show individual pivots; glow and touch count visualize local cluster density. This is candle-derived structure—not exchange order-book depth or guaranteed liquidity.

divergence.name: RSI divergences
divergence.body: Marks when price and RSI make different swing highs or lows. This describes a divergence in the selected data; it does not confirm exhaustion or time a reversal.

session.name: Session stats
session.body: Open/high/low/change of the running session plus range and annualised volatility — quick context on whether the day trends or meanders.

rv.name: Realised volatility
rv.body: Actually traded range, annualised. RV below IV = options price excitement the market has not yet delivered.

countdown.name: Candle countdown
countdown.body: Time remaining until the current candle closes. The final OHLCV values are set at close; values may change while the candle is forming.

patterns.name: Auto chart patterns
patterns.body: Looks for double tops/bottoms, head-and-shoulders patterns, triangles and flags in visible candle history. The confidence value is a heuristic fit score, not a probability of a future move.

ratings.name: MTF technicals
ratings.body: Combines 14 oscillator and moving-average readings from loaded data across six timeframes into a technical summary from Strong Sell to Strong Buy. It is not a trading recommendation; freshness depends on the data source.

heatmap.name: Market heatmap
heatmap.body: Treemap of the current provider-listed USDT ticker snapshot (Gate primary, OKX fallback): area = reported 24 h quote volume; colour = reported 24 h change. Missing changes stay neutral.

journal.name: Trade journal
journal.body: Local log of trades you enter, with win rate, profit factor, expectancy, average R, per-day stats and CSV export. These statistics summarize recorded trades; they do not establish a predictive edge.

magnifier.name: Bar magnifier
magnifier.body: Shows available trade prints within a candle: count, taker delta, cumulative delta and prints above $100k when supplied by the selected feed. Trade coverage can be partial.

replay.name: Bar replay
replay.body: Replays loaded candles bar by bar; indicators recalculate at each step using the visible replay window. This is historical replay, not a live feed.

backtest.name: Strategy Lab
backtest.body: Applies six rule-based strategies (EMA cross, RSI reversal, breakout and others) to the visible loaded history and reports trades, win rate, profit factor and equity curve. Results depend on data, fees and assumptions; they do not predict future performance.

screener.name: Screener
screener.body: Browse the current Gate USDT spot-ticker snapshot, with OKX as a fallback, by reported change, volume and range. Listings and fields vary by provider; missing changes stay blank. Includes filters, ad-hoc charts and CSV export.

customScripts.name: Script Lab
customScripts.body: Write your own per-candle indicator formulas (ema, rsi, vwap, …), test them, import from GitHub raw URLs and plot them as a line or price overlay.

scriptTopics.question: How do I write my own script?
scriptTopics.answer: Open Scripts in the terminal (or Custom script in the indicator modal). One formula per candle, e.g. ema(21) - ema(55) or c / vwap() - 1. Available: o h l c v plus ema(p) sma(p) rsi(p) atr(p) stoch(p) vwap() highest(p) lowest(p) change(p) and abs/max/min/sqrt/log/pow. Test shows last/min/max over the current buffer.

scriptTopics.question: How do I import scripts, e.g. from GitHub?
scriptTopics.answer: Paste an HTTPS URL into Script Lab; GitHub blob and Gist links are rewritten to raw URLs. The text loads into the editor (max 20 KB). Importing alone does not execute it; Test or Apply does. Formulas are not securely sandboxed and may access page/browser APIs and site data. Run only code you trust.

scriptTopics.question: How does the script land on the chart?
scriptTopics.answer: To the chart creates a CUSTOM indicator instance with your formula — as its own pane or (Overlay checkbox) directly on price. Saved scripts stay local in your browser and can be loaded, edited or deleted anytime.

edgeTopics.question: How does Liq Radar work?
edgeTopics.answer: Liq Radar looks at the last 400 candles of your chart and projects where positions leveraged 10x, 25x, 50x and 100x would hit their liquidation price. Candles with high volume and wide range count more and decay over time. The strongest clusters are drawn as magnet bands on the chart and listed in the Edge ▸ Liq Radar modal with distance and intensity. It is an estimate from your candles only – no exchange data, no guarantee.

edgeTopics.question: What does the Lag Oracle measure?
edgeTopics.answer: The Lag Oracle compares your chart with a leader feed (default: BTC on a configured CEX). It estimates the historical candle offset, correlation, beta and hit rate of past leader jumps. A notice may appear when the leader moves at least 1.5 standard deviations and the current move differs from the historical relationship. The feed loads only while the modal is open; this sample-dependent alert is informational, not a forecast.

edgeTopics.question: How does the Regime Compass detect the market state?
edgeTopics.answer: The Regime Compass combines ADX, the ratio of short-term to long-term realized volatility, the slope of a 50-bar regression and – when available – funding, market breadth and liquidation volume. The result is one of five regimes: strong trend, weak trend, range, volatility expansion or liquidation storm, each with confidence and drivers. The tool suggestions switch on the matching chart tools directly.

edgeTopics.question: What does Clock Edge show?
edgeTopics.answer: Clock Edge groups loaded candles by UTC hour and weekday and reports historical win rates and average returns over the next four candles. Cells with at least 30 observations and t ≥ 2 are marked statistically notable by a heuristic; this does not show that a pattern will persist or predict future results.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern the use of NodeChart. By opening the app you accept them. They are deliberately short and written in plain language.

sections.heading: 1. Scope of the service
sections.body: NodeChart is a browser-based charting and market-data interface for cryptocurrencies. It provides visualisation of publicly available price data. NodeChart is not an exchange, not a broker, not a custodian and not a payment service.

sections.heading: 2. No financial services
sections.body: NodeChart does not execute orders, does not hold funds and has no access to your wallets or exchange accounts. Any trade you place happens on the third-party venue you connect to yourself, under that venue's own terms.

sections.heading: 3. Availability and changes
sections.body: The service is provided free of charge and on a best-effort basis. Features may be added, changed or removed at any time. Public data feeds depend on third-party providers, whose availability NodeChart does not control.

sections.heading: 4. Acceptable use
sections.body: You agree not to abuse the service, not to attempt to disrupt it, and not to resell it or present it as your own product. Scraping or hammering the upstream exchange endpoints through NodeChart in a way that violates their terms is prohibited.

sections.heading: 5. Intellectual property
sections.body: The NodeChart name, design and source code are the property of the developer. Third-party data and brand names belong to their respective owners and are used for identification purposes only.

sections.heading: 6. Liability
sections.body: Liability for intent and gross negligence remains unrestricted. Beyond that, liability for slight negligence is limited to typically foreseeable damage. Trading cryptocurrencies carries a risk of total loss for which NodeChart is not responsible.

sections.heading: 7. Governing terms
sections.body: If individual provisions are invalid, the remaining provisions stay in force. Changes to these terms will be published on this page together with an updated date.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: Please read this carefully before using NodeChart for any trading decision.

sections.heading: No investment advice
sections.body: All content on NodeChart — charts, indicators, numbers, layouts and text — is provided for informational and technical demonstration purposes only. Nothing here constitutes investment, legal, tax or financial advice, and nothing is a recommendation to buy or sell any asset.

sections.heading: No guarantee of accuracy
sections.body: Market data is requested from third-party sources and may be cached, delayed, incomplete, aggregated differently or simply wrong. NodeChart cannot and does not guarantee the accuracy, completeness or timeliness of any displayed value.

sections.heading: Risk of total loss
sections.body: Cryptocurrencies are highly volatile and largely unregulated. You can lose your entire capital. Leverage, perpetuals and liquidity-pool positions can lose more than you deposited. Never trade with money you cannot afford to lose.

sections.heading: Your own responsibility

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: No account is required. The site still sends technical request data to its host and market-data providers and, only if you allow optional ads, to advertising partners. The sections below describe these main flows.

sections.heading: No account required
sections.body: The current version has no registration, login or user-account database. This does not mean that no personal data is processed: hosting, market-data providers and advertising partners may process technical request data such as IP addresses as described below.

sections.heading: Browser storage
sections.body: Theme, language, chart layout, watchlist and last selected symbol are saved in your browser’s localStorage. The watchlist and layout are not uploaded to a user account. The ad choice is also stored in this browser for up to six months so the site can honor it; clearing browser storage resets that choice. The functional NEXT_LOCALE cookie may store your language preference.

sections.heading: Optional ads and third-party services
sections.body: If you allow optional ads, the site loads Adsterra ad-delivery scripts. They may receive your IP address and browser/device request data and may store or read the provider’s own cookies or similar identifiers. If you reject or have not chosen, the app does not load these ad-delivery scripts. Market-data requests continue separately. The Smartlink kit is served from this site; its sponsored partner destination opens only after you click a clearly labeled link. No first-party analytics service is configured in the app; this does not describe processing by hosting, advertising or data providers. See their privacy notices for their own practices.

sections.heading: Market-data providers
sections.body: Depending on the feature and provider, your browser may connect directly to a public API or WebSocket, or the request may use a narrowly scoped API route on this site. The provider or hosting service may process your IP address and technical request data. Their privacy notices apply to those requests; not all data paths are direct.

sections.heading: Custom scripts and imported formulas
sections.body: If you test or apply a custom/imported formula, it executes as JavaScript in the app page. It is not a secure sandbox and may access browser APIs and site data available to that page or make network requests. Only run code you trust. Importing a URL fetches text from the URL you provide; the text is not executed just by importing it. Saved formulas are stored in this browser.

sections.heading: Hosting and logs
sections.body: The app is hosted on Cloudflare's edge network. Cloudflare processes requests as a technical service provider and may keep standard server logs for security and abuse prevention. No application-level user tracking is configured.

sections.heading: Your rights and contact
sections.body: For privacy questions or requests about your information, contact the address in the footer. Hosting, market-data and advertising providers may process request data under their own responsibilities and policies; include enough detail for us to identify the relevant service and we will respond under applicable requirements.

EMA.name: EMA
EMA.hint: Weights recent candles more heavily – trend direction and dynamic support.

SMA.name: SMA
SMA.hint: Arithmetic mean over the period – smooth support and resistance.

BB.name: Bollinger Bands
BB.hint: Middle band is the SMA, outer bands are standard deviations away. A squeeze means low volatility.

RSI.name: RSI
RSI.hint: Momentum between 0 and 100 – above 70 overbought, below 30 oversold.

MACD.name: MACD
MACD.hint: Difference of two EMAs plus the signal line; the histogram shows the strength of the move.

ATR.name: ATR
ATR.hint: Volatility in price points – handy for stop distances.

STOCH.name: Stochastic
STOCH.hint: Compares the close with the trading range of the period.

SUPERTREND.name: Supertrend
SUPERTREND.hint: Trend-following line that flips sides on trend change (ATR × multiplier).

DONCHIAN.name: Donchian Channels
DONCHIAN.hint: Breakout channels: highest high & lowest low of the period.

STOCHRSI.name: Stochastic RSI
STOCHRSI.hint: Stochastic applied to RSI – far more sensitive than RSI alone.

OBV.name: On-Balance Volume
OBV.hint: Cumulates volume on up/down closes – the volume trend.

MFI.name: Money Flow Index
MFI.hint: RSI with volume (0–100): overbought/oversold including money flow.

CCI.name: Commodity Channel Index
CCI.hint: Deviation from the statistical mean price (±100 levels).

ADX.name: ADX / DMI
ADX.hint: ADX = trend strength; +DI/−DI = bullish/bearish directional force.

PSAR.name: Parabolic SAR
PSAR.hint: Dots that trail the price and act as a trailing stop.

TRIX.name: TRIX
TRIX.hint: Rate of change of a triple-smoothed EMA – filters noise.

PPO.name: PPO
PPO.hint: MACD in percent – momentum comparable across symbols.

DPO.name: Detrended Price Oscillator
DPO.hint: Price minus shifted SMA – exposes cycles without the trend.

BBPCT.name: Bollinger %B
BBPCT.hint: Where price sits inside the Bollinger bands (0–1).

AROON.name: Aroon
AROON.hint: How recent the period high/low is (0–100; crossovers = turning points).

ICHIMOKU.name: Ichimoku Cloud
ICHIMOKU.hint: Japanese full system: Tenkan, Kijun and the Kumo cloud (Span A/B).

VWAP.name: VWAP
VWAP.hint: Session volume-weighted average price – the institutional benchmark.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.sub: Answered briefly and honestly – by a single developer who would rather build features than paywalls.

items.q: Is NodeChart really free to use?
items.a: Yes. Charts, indicators, metrics and tools are available without an account or subscription in the current release. Optional advertising (only if allowed) and voluntary donations help cover operating costs; there is no subscription paywall.

items.q: Which exchange adapter IDs and chain aliases are configured?
items.a: NodeChart has 12 configured CEX adapter IDs and 33 canonical chain IDs with provider-name aliases for normalising DEX responses. This registry is not proof of live market coverage; actual markets and token-risk data vary by provider, region and token.

items.q: Can I write my own indicator scripts?
items.a: Yes. Script Lab accepts per-candle formulas and can test and plot them. You may save formulas locally or import text from an HTTPS URL such as GitHub. Importing loads text into the editor; it does not run it. Testing or applying code executes it in this page, without a secure sandbox, where it may access browser APIs or site data. Run only code you trust.

items.q: Where do my data and drawings live?
items.a: Theme, language, layout, watchlist and active symbol are stored in this browser. The ad choice is also stored locally for up to six months. Market-data requests go to public providers; optional Adsterra scripts load only after you allow them. Sponsored partner links are opened only after a click. There is no user-account database, but hosts and providers may process technical request data such as IP addresses.

items.q: What should I know when comparing charting tools?
items.a: NodeChart focuses on browser-based CEX/DEX charts and local analysis. Market-data coverage depends on provider access, region and rate limits. Other services differ in features, data and pricing; check each service's current information. This release of NodeChart is free to use and supported by optional ads (only if allowed) and donations.

For traders exploring CEX and DEX charts without an account: help is available for listed indicators, with order-flow, options and on-chain metrics where providers supply data. Coverage, freshness and tool scope vary.

edge.liqHow: Liq Radar estimates hypothetical 10x–100x liquidation-price zones from the latest 400 chart candles, weighted by candle range, volume and recency. It does not use exchange position data and is not a forecast; do not treat the zones as confirmed targets or stops.

edge.lagNeed: Loading leader feed – at least 60 candles required.
edge.lagCalm: No open leader impulse. The market is waiting.
edge.lagHow: The Lag Oracle measures by how many candles the leader (e.g. BTC on Binance) has historically moved your chart, and reports live when a leader jump has only been partly followed. Pure statistics from public candles.
edge.lagPendingText: {leader} jumped {dir}{bps} bps – expectation {dir}{exp} bps for your coin, only {dir}{done} bps covered so far.
edge.regimeSub: Which market is running – and which tools fit
edge.regimeNeed: Not enough candles to classify yet.
edge.rdTrendStrong: The loaded sample shows high ADX and a clear fitted slope. These are trend-context measurements, not trade instructions.
edge.rdTrendWeak: Direction is less clear in the loaded sample. Review other data and indicators; this is not an entry or target recommendation.
edge.rdRange: The loaded sample is classified as range-bound. Volume zones are calculated from chart candles and are not guaranteed support or resistance.
edge.rdVolExpand: Realized volatility has risen without a clear trend in the available candles. This observation is not a position-sizing recommendation.
edge.rdLiqStorm: Funding and liquidation inputs are elevated in the available feed. Review the chart-based estimates as context, not as a price forecast.
edge.clockSub: Seasonality from your own chart data

edge.clockNowNo: No statistically notable pattern in the loaded sample for the current hour.
edge.clockLegend: Green = positive, red = negative average return of the next 4 candles; intensity = t-value, faded = not significant. Computed only from your loaded candles.
